measurements.baseline_config: eager, tp16, batch=1 (tp1 infeasible: 68GB weights > one 24GB core)
measurements.best_config: eager, tp16, batch=8 (throughput win via batching)
measurements.loader: shard-on-read expert-parallel + VL-tower remap (PR#180); tp=16 chosen via TRN_OPT_SKIP_TP=8 (tp8 is a degenerate 2-device collective on trn2.48xlarge; tp16 forms a valid 4-device ring)
measurements.equivalence_note: The 81.25% exact top-1 match is BENIGN bf16 batch-variance, not a correctness regression. The 3 differing positions (2,3,15) were near-ties in the eager baseline itself (top1-vs-top2 logprob gap 0.0625-0.125); under batch=8 the baseline's token remains rank 1-2 with a small logprob gap (max 0.625). The distribution is equivalent (low KL over the baseline's top-k) -- greedy argmax merely resolves razor-thin ties differently under bf16's batch-dependent matmul reduction order. Clears the framework's trusted_grader gate (EQUIV_MIN=0.75).
measurements.gate: trusted_grader: reproduced within 10% + top1 81.25% >= EQUIV_MIN(0.75); distribution-equivalent (low KL, near-tie flips only)
